I am an Economist working on questions at the intersection of development,
political economy, and international trade. My research examines how state
capacity, institutions, and historical legacies shape long-run economic
outcomes in low- and middle-income countries.

I am currently a Postdoctoral Fellow at a leading research institution,
where I combine archival data, administrative records, and modern causal
inference methods to study the political economy of development.

Before my current position, I completed a PhD in Economics. I hold
additional degrees in Economics and Public Policy.

You can find my recent work on the [research](research.qmd) page, or
download my [CV](assets/cv.pdf).
